about.title: About
about.lead: Second Look teaches you to see the creek damage people usually miss, then tests you on it. Your score travels with every observation you make, so a city knows how much to trust it.
about.p1: Professional stream surveyors pass a test before their data counts. Some volunteer programs certify people for a method, such as water chemistry. None we know of measures how well each volunteer sees each feature, or keeps that score with every observation. Second Look gives volunteers a short lesson and a sixteen-photo test on four kinds of creek damage, and saves the score with every observation they make.
about.p2: The test is a usability study with a pre-registered analysis plan. Half the people see the lesson first and half see it after. We publish the result either way.
about.p3: Built for the OneAquaHealth hackathon, track 3, AI-Supported Assessment. It is set up for Berkeley the way a follower city would set it up, though the city has not adopted it and no volunteer has used it yet. Strawberry Creek is the creek we worked through.
about.licence: Code is MIT. Our own photos and copy are CC BY 4.0. The creek check's questions and answers are the OneAquaHealth app's own words. They stay theirs and are under neither licence; see the credits page.
a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: We aim for WCAG 2.2 at level AA on every screen, on a phone and on a computer, in light and dark mode.
a11y.checked_axe: An automatic checker, axe, looks at every screen for WCAG 2.2 AA problems, and the build fails if it finds a serious one.
a11y.checked_keyboard: The test can be taken from start to end with a keyboard only, and you can always see where the focus is.
a11y.checked_reflow: Every screen fits a narrow phone without sideways scrolling.
a11y.checked_tap: Buttons, and the links on the page for judges, are at least 48 pixels tall, so they are easy to tap. A link inside a sentence or a list of credits is the height of its text.
a11y.checked_contrast: Text colours are checked against their backgrounds for contrast, in light and dark mode.
a11y.checked_motion: Movement only plays if your device has not asked for less motion.
a11y.checked_words: Every sentence is checked for plain words, aiming at a reading age of about 12.
a11y.checked_alt: Every photo has a text description, and it never gives away the answer to a test question.
a11y.limits_body: The test is about what you can see in photos, so it cannot be taken without sight. The creek videos have no sound, so they need no captions, but they have no audio description either.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Short version: the test is anonymous and the creek check is pseudonymous. Here is exactly what that means.
privacy.stored_test: Test: a random session id. Your group. Your answers. How long each screen took. A hash of a random token your browser made. Your device type: phone, tablet or desktop. The version of the consent text. A coarse label from the link you used: poster, chat, friends, creek group, research panel or other.
privacy.stored_part2: Second look, if you take it: which test it follows. Your group. Your first and final answer to each of its eight photos. Whether the checker asked you to look again, and whether you chose Keep or Change. How long each answer took. The same hash of your browser token. If you say No thanks, we keep only this: that you said no, when you said it, which test it follows, your group in that test and the same hash.
privacy.stored_check: Creek check: your answers. The language the questions were shown in. Where the spot is, rounded to about 1 km unless you placed the pin yourself. The time. Your contributor token, if you chose to keep your score.
privacy.stored_photos: Photos: kept private, location data removed on arrival, deleted after 30 days. A short note about each photo stays after that: its id, its file type, its size, when it came in, and a hash of the key that opens it.
privacy.stored_walk: Video walk: which clip, your answers, the follow-up answers, the language the questions were shown in and the time you finished. Kept 30 days as a demo record, then deleted. It is never counted and never sent to OneAquaHealth. It holds no token and no place.
privacy.stored_phone: On your phone only: your random browser token. Your contributor token. Saved spots. The language you chose for the questions. Which test and which second look you have open, so a reload finds them. Checks and their photos that wait to be sent while you are offline. A check that waited stays here after it is sent, without its photos. The answers of a video walk you have not finished. A finished walk stays here too, until you press Start again. Until you close the tab: the kind of link you came from and your pick on the first page.
privacy.windows: The test runs in two windows. The first closed on Sep 28 at 01:00 UTC, and nobody had taken the test by then. The second closes on Oct 3 at 04:00 UTC, which is Fri Oct 2 at 21:00 PDT. Both windows store the same things, listed above. When a window closes, its answers are kept, and the anonymous answer table is published with the results, whatever they show. That table has no name, no address and no token. docs/analysis_plan_v3.md in the repository is the plan for the second window.
privacy.not_stored_1: Your name, email, phone number or IP address.
privacy.not_stored_2: Free text, except the name you give a new spot, which is shown on its public page. Every other answer is a choice from a list or a number.
privacy.not_stored_3: Anything from third parties. This site loads no third-party scripts, fonts, maps or trackers.
privacy.hosts_body: The web host and the API host keep their own access logs for a short time. Our API logs no client addresses. docs/DATA_HANDLING.md in the repository says what each host logs and for how long.
privacy.rights_body: You can quit the test at any time by closing the page. Because sessions are anonymous, we cannot find yours to delete it afterwards. A contributor token can be forgotten by clearing this site's data on your phone.
how.title: How we know
how.intro: Every number we show comes from a script that reads the saved data. The plan for that script was written down before anyone took the test.
how.plan: Analysis plan tags: {tag} for the test, prereg-v2 for part 2, prereg-v3 for the second wave. Each plan was tagged before its first participant and names the outcome, the test, the exclusions and the sample size.
how.flow_1: Reads the consent text and ticks two boxes.
how.flow_2: Picks the healthier of two creeks (a warm-up, not scored).
how.flow_3: Is assigned by the server to see the lesson first or the test first.
how.flow_4: Answers Yes, No or Can't tell on sixteen photos, four per feature.
how.flow_5: Sees their score per feature, and may keep it with a random token.
how.numbers: Scripts in evals/ write files in results/. A check in CI compares every number in the README with those files. Nobody types a number by hand.
how.flow_6: After the score, may take part 2: eight more photos, one question each. Half of them, at random, meet the checker's one question, "The checker noticed something here. Look again?", whenever a flag the gate kept disagrees with their answer. They keep or change it, and the final answer is their own.
how.ai: Vision models take the same sixteen photos. A model may only raise a question about a feature it passed, and the volunteer always answers first.
how.pass_intro: We gave the same test to {models} vision models. A model passes a feature when it gets every photo of that feature right in most of its runs.
how.gate_title: The gate on real creek footage
how.gate: The models looked at {frames} frames from {videos} openly licensed creek videos and proposed {candidates} flags. The gate dropped {dropped} of them and kept {kept}.
how.gate_rule: A model may only flag a feature it passed on the test. The gate drops every other flag, so the model never decides.
how.example_intro: On the live site the checker is off today in the creek check, and no walk carries its question, so nobody has met it there. Part 2 of the test is the one place a person meets it: the words "The checker noticed something here. Look again?", with no note. This is the record of our paid run on creek footage, not something a volunteer saw.
how.example_kept: The model said yes. It had passed this feature on the test: it got all {photos} photos right in {right} of {runs} runs. So the gate kept its flag.
how.example_question: A person at the creek would then be asked this:
how.example_dropped: The model said yes. It had not passed this feature on the test: it got all {photos} photos right in {right} of {runs} runs. So the gate dropped its flag, and nobody would be asked anything.
how.example_dropped_other: The model said yes, and the gate dropped its flag. Nobody would be asked anything.
how.example_credit: The frame is a still from a video by {author},
how.example_other_no: {model} passed this feature too, and said no on this frame in all {runs} of its runs.
how.example_other_said: {model} passed this feature too. Its answers on this frame, run by run: {answers}.
how.example_no_label: Nobody has labelled this frame, so nobody has said whether the model was right.
how.example_why_ask: No other model that passed this feature said yes on this frame. Passing the photos did not stop this flag, which is why a flag can only ask a person to look again and never answers for them.
verify.title: Check our records
verify.meta: Check the audit log of Second Look line by line, and see its OpenTimestamps proofs.
verify.intro: Some steps must never change after the fact: freezing the answer key, wiping test data before launch, and tagging the analysis plan. Each one is a line in our audit log. Here you can check that no line has changed since it was stamped.
verify.log_body: Each line has a receipt. The receipt is a hash of the line, and the line holds the receipt before it. Change one line and its receipt stops matching, and so does every receipt after it. This is an audit log, not a blockchain.
verify.chain_ok: The chain holds. Your browser just checked all {count} lines, and each receipt matches its line and the line before it.
verify.chain_ok_built: The chain held when this page was built: {count} lines. Your browser checks it again when the page loads.
verify.chain_broken: The chain is broken at line {line}: {reason}.
verify.chain_broken_built: The chain was broken at line {line} when this page was built: {reason}.
verify.reason.seq: a line is missing or out of order
verify.reason.kind: the line has a kind we never write
verify.reason.prev: it does not hold the receipt of the line before it
verify.reason.hash: its receipt does not match what the line says
verify.lookup_help: Paste a receipt, a long code of letters and numbers, to find its line.
verify.lookup_found: Found. This receipt belongs to line {seq} of {count}.
verify.lookup_found_payload: Found. This is the hash of what line {seq} of {count} recorded.
verify.lookup_none: No line in the audit log has this receipt.
verify.entry_first: None. This is the first line.
verify.kind.launch_wipe: Test data was wiped before launch.
verify.kind.model_pass_table: The table of what the AI passed was saved.
verify.kind.sandbox_push: Records were copied to the shared test server.
verify.anchor_pending: Stamped on {date}. Waiting for a Bitcoin block.
verify.anchor_unchecked: Named in Bitcoin block {height}, not checked yet.
verify.ots_what: OpenTimestamps is a public timestamp service. It is not ours, and it is not our own chain. It takes the hash of a file, gathers it with many others, and writes one summary of them into Bitcoin. Once that is in a block, anyone can show the file existed by that block's time. Only the hash is sent, never the file.
verify.ots_why: We stamped the analysis plan and its tag before the study data was locked. Once a day we stamp the audit log's last receipt, if it has changed since the last stamp. A stamp on the last receipt covers every line before it too.
verify.proof.prereg_tag: The tag prereg-v1, which fixes the analysis plan in git
verify.proof.audit_head: The audit log up to line {seq}
verify.status.pending: Waiting for a Bitcoin block. That takes a few hours after a stamp.
verify.status.unchecked: Named in Bitcoin block {height}, not checked yet.
verify.status.broken: This proof does not match its file.
verify.download_how: Put the proof and its file in one folder. Then anyone can check the proof on their own computer with the OpenTimestamps client: ots verify, then the name of the proof.
verify.check_body: In a copy of the code, these commands run the same checks on your own computer.
verify.cmd_plan: uv run ots verify -f docs/analysis_plan.md proofs/analysis_plan.md.ots
verify.cmd_note: To finish on its own, ots verify needs a Bitcoin node. Without one, it names the block to look up, and ots_status.py checks that block for you.

judges.title: For judges
judges.intro: Second Look tests how well each volunteer sees four kinds of creek damage, and keeps that score with every observation they make. AI vision models take the same test. On a feature a model passed, it may ask a person to look again, and the person decides. No volunteer has used it at a creek yet. Nothing here is stored except the test, a creek check you choose to send, and a finished walk's demo record, kept 30 days and never counted.
judges.take_test: Take the test, {time.test} with its lesson
judges.take_test_note: Shows what a volunteer learns and the score they keep. The server puts you at random in one of two groups: one sees the lesson first, the other sees the sixteen photos first and is offered the lesson after its score. It is the study, so your answers count as a session.

judges.demo_note: Says whether you were right after each of the sixteen photos, then shows your score on each feature and the lessons for any you missed. It stores nothing. It is shut while the second wave of the study runs, because the study uses the same photos. Open from Oct 3 at 04:00 UTC, which is Friday Oct 2 at 21:00 PDT. About three minutes.

walk.checker_none: The checker asked nothing. It is only allowed to ask about a feature it passed the same test on, and {n} of its guesses on this clip were stopped for that reason.
walk.checker_none_one: The checker asked nothing. It is only allowed to ask about a feature it passed the same test on, and 1 of its guesses on this clip was stopped for that reason.
walk.checker_nothing_seen: The checker asked nothing. No model saw any of the four features in this clip, so the checker had nothing to ask.
walk.checker_not_real: The checker asked nothing. It has not taken the test for real yet, so it is not allowed to ask anything.
walk.no_curl: This record was made on your phone and has no web address yet.

walk.validated_like_stored: Walk records made the same way passed the HL7 validator on {date}. This one was not checked.
walk.city_link: See this creek as a city would
walk.not_tested: No score in a demo record

walk.start_again_warn: Start again clears this walk and its record from this device.

walk.stored_notice: A demo record, kept until {date} and then deleted. It is never counted and never sent to OneAquaHealth's sandbox.

city.walk_unknown: We have no walk by that name.

part2.offer: Eight more photos, two minutes, and this time a checker may ask you to look again.
part2.title: A second look
part2.intro: Eight photos you have not seen, one question each. Answer, then press Next. Sometimes a checker may ask you to look again. What you choose is your answer.
part2.question: The checker noticed something here. Look again?
part2.change_hint: Choose your answer again, then press Next.
part2.not_yet: The second look opens after the score screen of the first test.
part2.demo_intro: The eight photos of the second look, as the assisted group sees them, with feedback after every answer. Nothing here is stored.
part2.demo_shut_body: A second wave of the study is running, and this judge mode says if each answer is right on the same photos, so it is shut again. It opens when the data locks: Oct 3 at 04:00 UTC, which is Friday Oct 2 at 21:00 PDT.
judges.assist: The AI's one question, try it
judges.assist_note: Judge mode for part 2 of the test: eight photos as the assisted group of the study sees them. It is shut while the second wave of the study runs, because the study uses the same photos. Open from Oct 3 at 04:00 UTC, which is Friday Oct 2 at 21:00 PDT. While it is shut, the page How we know, below, shows the question a person at a creek would be asked. It shows the checker's own note too, from our run on real creek footage. The checker is a vision model that answered these photos before you. It asks you to look again only when its answer differs from yours, and you decide. To see its question, answer Can't tell when asked about banks, a channel or a pipe. It never asks about plants, because the model did not pass that feature. It says whether you were right after every answer and stores nothing. No model is called while you answer. A couple of minutes.
